<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par52 />even in {{GHGterm|pause}}; cf. {{GHGpar|29|s}} and 65 e. In the 1st sing. imperfect the ''e''-sound occurs in two words for {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}}, under the preformative {{GHGheb|text=א}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֱזָרֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=12|verse=14|hidebook=1}} and {{GHGheb|text=וְאֵסָ֣עֲרֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=14}} (in accordance with {{GHGpar|23|h}}).—Before the full plural ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} (see {{GHGpar|47|m}}) the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} is retained in {{GHGterm|pause}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תְּדַבֵּר֑וּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=2}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּדַבְּר֣וּן}}), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=12|verse=3}}; so before ''Silluq'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=58|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=11}} and even before {{GHGterm|Zaqeph qaṭon}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=5}}. Instead of {{GHGheb|text=תְּקַטֵּ֫לְנָה}}, forms like {{GHGheb|text=תְּקַטַּ֫לְנָה}} are also found, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, in both cases before a sibilant and in pause. Also {{GHGheb|text=פַּלַּג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=10}} occurs as the 2nd sing. imperative (probably an intentional imitation of the sound of the preceding {{GHGheb|text=בַּלַּע}}) and {{GHGheb|text=קָרַב}} (for ''qarrabh'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=17}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|o}}
3. The ''infinite absolute'' of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} has sometimes the special form {{GHGheb|text=קַטֹּל}} given in the paradigm, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יַסֹּר|translate=castigando}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=18}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=10}} (from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=2}} (from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}); but much more frequently the form of the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} ({{GHGheb|text=קַטֵּל}}) is used instead. The latter has also, in exceptional cases, the form {{GHGheb|text=קִטֵּל}} (with ''ă'' attenuated to ''ĭ'' as in the {{GHGterm|perfect}}), e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=8|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלְחוֹ}}; perhaps also (if not a substantive) {{GHGheb|text=קִטֵּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=21}}; and for the sake of assonance even for {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=נִאֵץ נִאַ֫צְתָּ}}). On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלֵּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=35}} and {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֵּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=13}} are better regarded as substantives, while {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֶּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=6|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=15}} (in each case after {{GHGheb|text=בְּיוֹם}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=1|verse=2}} (after {{GHGheb|text=תְּחִלַּת}}), in all of which places it is considered by König (after Qimḥi) to be {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}}, is really perfect of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|p}}
The infinitive construct {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, with the {{GHGterm|fem.}} ending (cf. {{GHGpar|45|d}}), occurs in {{GHGheb|text=יַסְּרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=זַמְּרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=147|verse=1}}; with {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of the {{GHGterm|fem.}} before a suffix {{GHGheb|text=צַדֶּקְתֵּךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=52}}. On the verbal nouns after the form of the Aram. inf. ''Pa‛il'' ({{GHGheb|text=קַטָּלָה}}), see {{GHGpar|84|e|b}}.

Instead of the abnormal {{GHGheb|text=מְאָֽסְפָיו}} (so Baer, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=62|verse=9}}) as ptcp. Pi‛el, read {{GHGheb|text=מְאַסְ׳}} with ed. Mant. and Ginsburg.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|q}}
4. In Puʿal ''ŏ'' is sometimes found instead of ''ŭ'' in the initial syllable, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מְאָדָּם|translate=dyed red}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=25|verse=5}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=4}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=7|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁדְּדָה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=72|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=11|hidebook=1}}. According to Baer’s reading also in {{GHGheb|text=תְּרָצְּחוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=4}}, and so also Ben Ašer, but Ben Naphtali {{GHGheb|text=תְּרַצְּחוּ}}. It is merely an orthographic licence when ''ŭ'' is written fully, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יוּלַּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=29}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|r}}
5. As {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} of {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} we find {{GHGheb|text=גֻּנֹּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=15}}.—No instance of the ''inf. constr.'' occurs in the strong verb in {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}; from {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} with suffix {{GHGheb|text=עֻנּוֹתוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=132|verse=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|s}}
6. A few examples occur of the {{GHGterm|participle Puʿal}} without the preformative ({{GHGheb|text=מְ‍}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֻכָּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=יוּלָּד}} (for {{GHGheb|text=מְיֻלָּד}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֻקָּח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=2|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=סֹעֲרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=11}}. These {{GHGterm|participles}} are distinguished from the {{GHGterm|perfect}} (as in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}) by the ''ā'' of the final syllable. For other examples, see {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=12}} (where {{GHGheb|text=יוּקָשִׁים}}, according to {{GHGpar|20|n}}, stands for {{GHGheb|text=יֻקָּ׳}} = {{GHGheb|text=מְיֻקָּ׳}}); but, according to the Masora, ''not'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=17}}, since {{GHGheb|text=הַֽהֻלָּ֫לָה}} as ''Mil‛êl'' can only be the {{GHGterm|perfect}}. The rejection of the {{GHGheb|text=מְ‍}} may be favoured by an initial {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=2.7}} (but also {{GHGheb|text=מְמֻשָּׁךְ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=19}} (where, however, read {{GHGheb|text=מוֹעֶ֫דֶת}}); so also in the participle {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=מָאֵן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=7|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=2|hidebook=1}} (always after {{GHGheb|text=אִם}}, but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=הַמֵּאֲנִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=10}}, where, however, {{GHGheb|text=הַמָּֽאֲנִים}} = {{GHGheb|text=הַמְמָֽאֲנִים}} is to be read, with Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 264 f.) and {{GHGheb|text=מַהֵר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=1|verse=14}} (and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=1.3}}?). Notice, however, Barth’s suggestion ({{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, p. 273) that, as the active of forms like {{GHGheb|text=אֻכָּל}} only occurs in {{GHGterm|Qal}}, they are perfect participles of former ''passives'' of Qal (see e), and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=32|hidebook=1}}, perfect participles of Piʿēl.—On {{GHGheb|text=מְרֻבַּע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=45|verse=2}}, see {{GHGpar|65|d}}.<section end=par52 /><noinclude>
